title: The Lit Trail
lens: a directed journey with rich side branches (Ori WotW's Inkwater Marsh into Wellspring, Nine Sols' opening): a strong forward pull, set pieces with quiet between them, side branches that loop back ahead of where they left
pitch: Wing hatches last and spends the whole wood chasing the tail of her swarm. The last firefly is always one step ahead of her, hanging fresh lights along the tail's path and snaring it a knot of moths at a time. Its lights lead the tail, and her, to the Lamp Loom: the wood's great lamp, a gold blaze under the canopy that she can see from the first vista on, where an orb-weaver has strung its web between the firefly's flames. The main line is a pursuit built from set pieces with quiet between them. She runs the canopy after the river of moths, leaps off the lip as her wings open over the valley, and chases the Kindling as lamps flare on ahead of her one by one. Then she falls into silent black roots, finds the rock that breathes, climbs a hollow trunk by claw with the old burrback ramming it below, and bursts out into moonlight on the high boughs. The web gauntlet and the Weaver end it, and the Mooring opens as the area's hub. Six side branches hang off the line. Each is visible from it and each rejoins it further on, so curiosity never costs a walk back: a loft above the hatch, a cellar with the map, a hard fling gauntlet for sharp wings, a gallery of wings under the roots, the firefly's own cache, and the old burrback's den. It's fun because something you care about is always ahead and pulling, moths you can see getting caught, and something is always beside you, tempting you off the line.
throughline: Catch the tail of her swarm before the firefly's trail of lights leads every last moth into the web at the Lamp Loom.

regions.name: The Cocoon Bough
regions.note: The row of split cocoons high in the west, and control at 8 s. Tatter is on the branch with one wing torn, and the swarm pours past the moon. The camera leads east, but the bough also runs west into a curled leaf (glow, and a picked glowcap stump), and the dead cocoons overhead hang in a row she can pogo up into the loft. Dense: a leaf to cut, a row to climb, the way east.

regions.name: The Cocoon Loft
regions.note: The wrong way pays first. Up on the canopy top: a ring of picked glowcap stumps (firefly sign 1, its call plays once when she stands still), two wicks holding a knot of moths, glow pods, and the highest view in the area, the firefly hanging a light far off to the east. It runs east above the chase and drops her onto the lip, ahead of where she left.

regions.name: The Swarm Road
regions.note: Set piece 1: a downhill run east along the canopy's limbs with the river of moths overhead, keyed to her x so it never escapes and never waits. No enemies. Leaf curtains to cut through at a run (they spill glow), twig bridges that dip under her, two forks (a high twig line with pods, a low bough that's safer), gaps that grow. She can't glide yet, so a miss drops her onto a lower limb, never out of the run.

regions.name: Lampfall Lip
regions.note: The canopy breaks on a lip over the wood. A look of 1.5 s at most, and she keeps control: the valley's lamps far to the east with the swarm breaking into knots around them, the moon over the mountain, and below, in the wood, a gold blaze under the trees with the stragglers (the Tail) peeling down toward it. The title appears over the moon. She jumps after them and her wings open in the moonlight: glide, one item line. Then two screens of falling with the Tail through drifting leaves, with glowcap clusters on the trunk to swipe on the way down.

regions.name: Straggler Dell
regions.note: The first lights. The Tail snags on a wick over a dip. Pressing Lamp near the flame stops time; she aims and launches, and the flame snuffs as she leaves it, its moths rejoining the Tail. Then a chain of two. Juvenile beetles (two cuts) in the leaf litter, glowcaps to hack, a wick behind a thorn band she can't reach yet, and a ring of dead moths on a hollow patch of floor (the cellar). Ahead, a warm light hangs a fresh wick and darts east: the firefly.

regions.name: The Glowcap Cellar
regions.note: Under the dell, through the hollow patch (three down-cuts, each a bounce). It's dark, with glowcaps everywhere to hack and two sleeping beetles that wake only in the light of the cellar's one wick. The moth-stone (the area's map) is here, carved with moths following a light. The cellar comes up under the trail through a bark lid that breaks from below: a shortcut ahead.

regions.name: The Firefly's Trail
regions.note: The firefly's fresh lamps are strung east through the trees, each with a knot of the Tail spinning in it. Two lines cross twice. The high line has fling chains and a hawker hunting the air between flames. The low line has beetles in the light pools and a dangler over the cut spot under a wick. P1 is at the start, with Tatter already resting there (it walked). Above, a lamp chain climbs into a thorn canopy; midway, the cellar's lid opens from below. Every screen has a lamp, a creature and something to cut, and always a second line.

regions.name: The Thorn Canopy
regions.note: The optional hard part: a fling gauntlet that climbs from the trail's high line into the thorns. It's in view from the main path: the challenge shows, the way through doesn't. Three checkpoints with the embers retry: two-flame chains, then a sharp change of angle with a glide between flames, then a swinging lantern. The reward is sharp wings (a fling's launch cuts whatever she passes), which changes every fight after it, the Weaver's included. It drops onto the Kindling's high ledge, ahead.

regions.name: The Kindling
regions.note: Set piece 2. In a long gallery under a fallen trunk, the firefly flies ahead hanging lamps, and they flare on one by one as she comes. The Tail swerves into each. She chases at full speed, fling to fling, snuffing as she launches, with a hawker diving at the chain and burrbacks in the pools below if she drops. There is no fail state: a lamp she hasn't reached holds its moths and waits, so falling behind only makes the rescue slower. The last lamp hangs over a clearing carpeted with dead moths. She lands, and the leaf lid gives way.

regions.name: The Breathing Roots
regions.note: The trough. Black and silent, with no lamps and no music: the Tail is gone for the first time and nothing pulls. Drips and root curtains, and the Loom's gold as a faint seam through ceiling cracks to the east. She walks a long, low, curved ledge that looks like rock. At the east end a hollow trunk rises, and its walls slide under her kicks: the lock, seen a minute before the key. A cold draft rises from one spot in the floor (the gallery).

regions.name: The Wing Gallery
regions.note: The old burrback's larder under the roots, its walls lined with moth wings and the pale stains of old migrations. The only light is a chain of three wicks over a black drop, with a dangler on the middle one. Here are firefly sign 2 (a string of glowcaps hung and abandoned) and a moonlit hollow: long breath (the fling's aim lasts twice as long). It climbs out through a root grate into the moonwell's floor, ahead.

regions.name: The Moonwell
regions.note: A shaft of real moonlight falls through the roots onto a mossy floor, the first since the lip. She basks and gets claws (wall jump), one item line. P2. A practice well of two faces has glowcaps at the top. The gallery's grate opens here. A root tunnel east is choked with rubble and old beetle scrapes: the den, which opens from its far side later.

regions.name: The Split Oak
regions.note: Set piece 3, the escape. Back at the trunk's foot the rock breathes: the ledge she walked was the old burrback asleep. It unfolds and charges. She kicks up the hollow trunk with her new claws while it rams the foot. Each ram is a beat that shakes bark plates loose above and breaks the chimney away below her. Two wicks in the shaft are fling boosts (and their moths), and a thorn band forces a kick across the shaft. Three screens and ~60 s, with the rams speeding up near the top. She bursts out of a knot-hole, and the foot caves in behind her.

regions.name: The High Boughs
regions.note: The quiet after: moonlight, and the music drops to wind. Looking back west, the hatching tree and the Swarm Road are far off. Ahead, the Loom's gold blaze lights the canopy from below and silk glitters on every branch (the spiders thicken toward the light). P3. Then crumbling bark bridges, with bombardiers on the ledges spitting arcs across them, lamps between, and glowcap pods. Below the bough line, one flame burns with no moths in it (the cache).

regions.name: The Firefly's Cache
regions.note: A hollow under the boughs full of the firefly's half-finished work: glowcaps strung but not hung, a ring of lights set out in its flash rhythm, and in the middle a lamp built in the shape of a firefly (the marsh's reveal, foreshadowed). A fling playground: flames everywhere, no thorns, pure flow. At the top is a moon-drop (+1 max health). It drops out into the middle of the silk gate.

regions.name: The Silk Gate
regions.note: The web gauntlet down to the Loom's door. Orb webs are strung across the lamp light, with weavers that run to wherever she touches. Tail moths are stuck in the strands (cutting each out is a small rescue). A bombardier sits behind a web, and a dangler hangs over the only standing spot. The great lamp's glow fills the bottom of the frame. P4 is at the door, with a heal before the fight.

regions.name: The Lamp Loom
regions.note: The wood's great lamp in a clearing, wrapped in an orb web strung between five of the firefly's flames, with the whole Tail spun into it. This is the Weaver's arena. Afterwards the canopy over it opens to the sky (the wood's first stars), the Tail bursts free, and a moon shaft falls: Gust. The firefly darts in, flashes its alarm and flees east. Dead moths drop through a root grate in the floor into the dark below (the den).

regions.name: The Old Den
regions.note: Under the Loom, where every moth that dies at the great lamp falls through the grate. After the escape the old burrback came back here, fat on them. It's an optional mini-boss in three phases: a brace only the pogo breaks, a roll broken by a fling-cut from the den's wick, and rams she baits into the taproot. The reward is a moon-drop. The tunnel is the shortcut: hub to moonwell in ~40 s.

regions.name: The Mooring
regions.note: The area's hub, at the wood's east edge over the valley: a moonlit pool and a pale fallen limb (the Moth Log) where the freed Tail settles to rest before the road. The firefly relit one wick on the log as it fled; Gusting it out is Gust's first payoff. The west tunnel is hung with silk: Gust tears it, and Tatter walks out of the dark and sits by her. Exits: east down the cliff into the valley (the next area); north, a ledge one jump too high (double jump, later); west, the den's shortcut back into the wood, where Gust now reaches the lamps left burning; down, a sealed root door (the drowned roots stub).

boss.name: The Weaver of the Loom
boss.idea: An orb-weaver has strung its web between five of the firefly's flames around the wood's great lamp, and the whole Tail is spun into it. It's the lab Weaver Matt liked, with one exam a phase, rebuilt around what this area taught. P1, the ring (the fling): the ring flames are the only anchors; each fling launch snuffs one and drops its spoke, Tail moths burst out of the falling strands, the heart's pull bends every flight, and the weaver runs along the web to wherever she touches it. P2, the drops (the claws): the web falls in sections, and the weaver drops on silk at points the thread shows first (as the danglers taught) and swings across half the arena, with the safe side always opposite; she kicks up the trunks to stay above it and cuts the thread when it hangs winded. P3, the floor (the pogo): the heart lowers, and the weaver lunges and lies winded with its abdomen up; only a pogo lands, and with sharp wings a fling through it staggers it. After 3 pogos it flees, and 3 hits put out the heart. Clear in ~2.5 min, ~75 s back to P3 on a retry, P4 15 s from the door. Ending: the canopy opens on the wood's first stars, the Tail bursts free, Gust is found in the moon shaft, and the firefly flashes its alarm and flees east.

minuteByMinute: 0–2: hatch (control at 8 s), the swarm over the moon, the Swarm Road chase east along the canopy, cutting leaf curtains at a run; the loft for the curious

2–4: the lip (the vista, the Loom's blaze, the title), the leap as her wings open (glide), down with the Tail into the dell; the first fling frees the first moths; the firefly is glimpsed hanging a light
4–6: the trail begins: P1 with Tatter; beetles in light pools, a dangler over a cut spot, the high line or the low line; the cellar's hollow floor and the thorn chain tempt
6–8: a hawker over the high line, the Loom's glow nearer through the gaps, the Split Oak rising ahead
8–9: the Kindling: lamps flare on ahead, a fling chain at full speed with a hawker diving at it; the leaf lid gives way
9–11: the roots, black and silent, with the Tail gone; walking the long curved rock; the slick trunk; the draft over the gallery
11–12: the Moonwell: claws; back to the trunk's foot
12–14: the rock breathes: the escape up the Split Oak with the old burrback ramming below; out through the knot-hole
14–16: the high boughs in moonlight and the look back west; bombardiers on crumbling bark; the cache's odd flame
16–17.5: the Silk Gate: webs, weavers, moths cut out of the strands; P4 and a heal at the door
17.5–21: the Weaver: the ring (fling), the drops (claws), the floor (pogo), the heart
21–23: the sky clears, the Tail is freed, Gust; the firefly flees east; the Mooring: Gust the relit wick, tear the silk, Tatter comes through, the valley below
